claims.text: What the image looks like Cord T2 hyperintensity with vertebral body abnormality compressing cord → metastatic spinal cord compression
claims.quote: Cord T2 hyperintensity with vertebral body abnormality compressing cord Metastatic spinal cord compression
claims.locator: MRI - When MRI > CT, findings table

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Spine: cord compression, cauda equina, disc herniation, spondylodiscitis
claims.quote: Spine: cord compression, cauda equina, disc herniation, spondylodiscitis.

claims.text: Suggested by spinal or radicular pain with reflex, motor or sensory deficits, particularly at a segmental level
claims.quote: Spinal cord compression is suggested by spinal or radicular pain with reflex, motor, or sensory deficits, particularly at a segmental level.

claims.text: MRI is done immediately if available; if unavailable, CT myelography: iohexol introduced via lumbar puncture runs cranially to check for complete block of the CSF
claims.quote: MRI is done immediately if available. If MRI is unavailable, CT myelography is done; a small amount of iohexol (a nonionic, low osmolar radiopaque agent) is introduced via a lumbar puncture and allowed to run cranially to check for complete block of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

claims.text: If traumatic bone abnormalities needing immediate spinal immobilization are suspected, spinal radiographs can be done, but CT detects bone abnormalities better
claims.quote: If traumatic bone abnormalities (eg, fracture, dislocation, subluxation) that require immediate spinal immobilization are suspected, spinal radiographs can be done. However, CT detects bone abnormalities better.

claims.text: Causes Compression is caused far more commonly by lesions outside the spinal cord (extramedullary) than by lesions within it (intramedullary)
claims.quote: Compression is caused far more commonly by lesions outside the spinal cord (extramedullary) than by lesions within it (intramedullary).

claims.text: Acute (minutes to hours): often trauma (eg, vertebral crush fracture, acute disc herniation, vertebral subluxation or dislocation) or metastatic tumor
claims.quote: Acute compression develops within minutes to hours. It is often due to Trauma (eg, vertebral crush fracture with displacement of fracture fragments, acute disc herniation, severe bone or ligamentous injury causing hematoma, vertebral subluxation or dislocation) Metastatic tumor

claims.text: Subacute (days to weeks): usually a metastatic extramedullary tumor, a subdural or epidural abscess or hematoma, or a cervical or, rarely, thoracic herniated disc
claims.quote: Subacute compression develops over days to weeks. It is usually caused by A metastatic extramedullary tumor A subdural or an epidural abscess or hematoma A cervical or, rarely, thoracic herniated disc

claims.text: Chronic (months to years): commonly bony protrusions into the spinal canal (eg, osteophytes or spondylosis), especially when the canal is narrow
claims.quote: Chronic compression develops over months to years. It is commonly caused by Bony protrusions into the cervical, thoracic, or lumbar spinal canal (eg, due to osteophytes or spondylosis, especially when the spinal canal is narrow, as occurs in spinal stenosis)

claims.text: Symptoms Acute or advanced compression: segmental deficits, paraparesis or quadriparesis, hyporeflexia (when acute) followed by hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses, loss of sphincter tone (bowel and bladder dysfunction) and sensory deficits
claims.quote: Acute or advanced spinal cord compression causes segmental deficits, paraparesis or quadriparesis, hyporeflexia (when acute) followed by hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses, loss of sphincter tone (with bowel and bladder dysfunction), and sensory deficits.

claims.text: Subacute or chronic compression may begin with local back pain, often radicular, and sometimes hyperreflexia and loss of sensation; sensory loss may begin in the sacral segments; complete loss of function may follow suddenly and unpredictably
claims.quote: Subacute or chronic compression may begin with local back pain, often radiating down the distribution of a nerve root (radicular pain), and sometimes hyperreflexia and loss of sensation. Sensory loss may begin in the sacral segments. Complete loss of function may follow suddenly and unpredictably, possibly resulting from secondary spinal cord infarction.

claims.text: Spinal percussion tenderness is prominent if the cause is metastatic carcinoma, abscess or hematoma
claims.quote: Spinal percussion tenderness is prominent if the cause is metastatic carcinoma, abscess, or hematoma.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: steroids, urgent radiation/surgery
claims.locator: MRI - When MRI > CT, findings table

claims.text: If compression causes neurologic deficits or pain, dexamethasone is given immediately, followed promptly by surgical decompression or radiation therapy; radiation can be used if the compression is from a radiosensitive tumor
claims.quote: If compression causes neurologic deficits or pain, dexamethasone is given immediately followed promptly by surgical decompression (1) or radiation therapy. Radiation therapy can be used if compression is from a radiosensitive tumor.

claims.text: Surgery is indicated when neurologic deficits worsen despite nonsurgical treatment, a biopsy is needed, the spine is unstable, tumors recur after radiation therapy, or an abscess or hematoma is compressing the cord
claims.quote: Surgery is indicated in the following cases: Neurologic deficits worsen despite nonsurgical treatment. A biopsy is needed. The spine is unstable. Tumors recur after radiation therapy. An abscess or a subdural or epidural hematoma is compressing the spinal cord.

claims.text: Incomplete or very recent complete loss of function may be reversible, but complete loss of function rarely is; for acute compression, diagnosis and treatment must occur immediately
claims.quote: Incomplete or very recent complete loss of function may be reversible, but complete loss of function rarely is; thus, for acute compression, diagnosis and treatment must occur immediately.
